summary: Cross-tenant service impersonation fails due to Okta group namespace truncation in identity proxy
description:
Issue summary: Internal service-to-service impersonation that relies on Okta group claims is failing when the impersonated principal has long namespaced groups. The identity proxy appears to truncate or drop group entries containing namespace separators (e.g., org:team:role), causing RBAC evaluation to deny impersonation.

Observed since 2026-03-10 07:40 UTC during the nightly runbook sweep. Affected operators cannot escalate runbooks that require cross-tenant impersonation and several CI jobs that create ephemeral service tokens are failing with 403.

Impact: High — oncall runbook escalation and scheduled internal automations are blocked. Manual workarounds are slow and error-prone.

Initial triage: Reproducible with a manual curl that includes a long X-Impersonate-Groups header. Short group lists succeed; long namespaced groups are either truncated or completely missing when they arrive at the auth service for RBAC evaluation.
impact: Multiple internal runbooks blocked, CI-scheduler failing ~8% of nightly jobs, oncall escalation fallback being used. Estimated to affect 12 teams in us-east.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a service account A that will impersonate user B with groups that include namespaced entries (example: org:platform:runbooks, org:platform:ci-runners, org:infra:admin).
2) From the identity-proxy edge, POST to /v1/impersonate with header: X-Impersonate-Subject: service-A and X-Impersonate-Groups: org:platform:runbooks,org:platform:ci-runners,org:infra:admin
3) Observe response from auth service: 403 with RBAC deny. Check received headers at auth: the X-Impersonate-Groups header is shortened to "org:platform:runb..." or missing namespaced segments.
4) Repeat with a non-namespaced group list (team-members, infra-admin) and request succeeds.
5) Reproduce intermittently by increasing the total character length of group header; failures correlate with header byte length and presence of ':' characters.
logs: identity-proxy (2026-03-10T07:42:11Z): incoming headers size=734 bytes, X-Impersonate-Groups="org:platform:runbo"
auth-service (2026-03-10T07:42:12Z): RBAC decision DENY - missing required group org:platform:runbooks for impersonation request from svc-ci
nginx-proxy (2026-03-10T07:42:11Z): client_header_buffer_size=128, client_max_header_size=4096 (observed truncation when combined with internal rewrite)
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: identity-proxy or one of the upstream proxies has a header-size/encoding bug that truncates values containing ':' (namespace separator).
Checked proxy config: nginx edge has client_header_buffer_size set to 128 for legacy vhost used by some internal tenants — likely inherited from an old template.

Captured raw TCP between proxy and auth: header bytes are truncated before reaching auth-service; observed truncation point aligns with 128-byte buffer boundary when long namespaced group strings are present.
Tested bypass: hit auth-service directly (bypassing proxy) with full X-Impersonate-Groups header — RBAC succeeds. Confirms proxy-level mutation.
Triage action: increased client_header_buffer_size temporarily to 2k on staging vhost and validated that impersonation with namespaced groups succeeds consistently.
Risk assessment: change to edge nginx template impacts many internal vhosts; need controlled rollout and verification for potential memory/latency impacts.

Next steps: prepare PR to update nginx vhost template to conservative buffer sizes, add unit tests for header pass-through, and add regression alerts for header truncation errors in identity-proxy metrics.
